newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Malaysia blue-chips rebound in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Malaysia blue-chips rebound in morning trade.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares staged a strong rebound in the morning session on Wednesday, but analysts and fund managers said the move was mainly technically driven after two days of sharp falls.
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks stood 15.27 points, or 1.7 percent, higher at 912.52. It had peaked at 919.58.

"The rebound is not that great when you consider that the index has fallen around 30 points over the last few days. It is just coming back to its previous levels," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at SJ Securities.
The index has lost 35.11 points, or 3.76 percent, since last Friday, and has shed more than 25 percent this year.

Dealers and analysts said local and foreign institutional investors had been seen selectively buying large-capitalised issues such as Telekom Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd. The stocks gained 30 and 20 cents, respectively.
Power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd were also actively traded, gaining 30 cents and 10 cents respectively.
The four stocks together have a 44 percent weightage on the Composite Index.
"There has been some local (institutional) buying. There has been some nibbling by foreigners, but they are still net sellers," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.

Some dealers and analysts attributed the rebound to statements by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Tuesday that the government may defer some large infrastructure projects to reduce the country's current account deficit.
He was responding to fears expressed by economists that Malaysia's economy may be overheating.
But earlier comments by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad indicating that he would continue to pursue a high-growth economic policy were seen as contradictory to Anwar's statements, said analysts.
"They have to stop contradicting each other. If nothing is done I see the market going down further," said a senior foreign fund manager in Kuala Lumpur.
"Everything is a moving target at the moment. There have been conflicting statements about important matters which have affected the confidence of local and foreign investors," he said.
Underlying concerns over the direction of the ringgit continued to erode the possibility of a sustained rebound.
"This is a short-term rebound. I'm inclined to believe it is not sustainable. We are not quite out of the woods yet; there are still concerns over the ringgit," said Faez.
Anwar said on Tuesday that Malaysia would not defend the ringgit against speculative attacks.
The ringgit was expected to stay weak against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday, trading within a range of between 2.7600 and 2.8500, traders said.
The currency closed at 2.7645/75 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday after hitting a new 42-month low of 2.7930 during the session.
